_readme: Source of truth for /artifacts. Edit this file, then run: python3 scripts/build-artifacts.py
_style: Write for someone who has never used crypto. No jargon (bricked, mint(), proof-of-work, onchain, pool, decimals). Mining is fine when explained: say 'mines' or 'mining rewards', never 'payouts'. If a technical idea matters, explain it in everyday words.

artifacts.name: 0xDOGE Token
artifacts.oneLiner: The first copy of 0xBitcoin. A bug stopped mining for good after just 12 rewards, so no new coins can ever be made.
story: 0xDOGE launched on February 16, 2018, just 10 days after 0xBitcoin. 0xBitcoin was a coin on Ethereum that people earned by having their computers solve math puzzles, the same way Bitcoin works. This is called mining: every solved puzzle earns a mining reward of new coins. 0xDOGE was the first copy of it.

Then it sat untouched for 8 years. In May 2026 it was finally mined, and after just 12 successful mines it broke for good. Two mistakes in its code were to blame: one in how mining rewards were calculated, and one in a built-in limit that tripped over itself. Nobody can mine new coins from it, and nobody ever will.
That left exactly 1.2 million coins in existence, with no way to make more. 0xDOGE was the first coin of its kind on Ethereum to permanently break itself.

supply.label: No more can ever be made

facts: 9 trillion, a limit it will never reach
